findings.title: Global Idempotency Middleware Cross-User Response Hijacking and Auth Bypass
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-287 / CWE-639 / OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
findings.exploit_path: 1) middleware.Idempotency(rdb, 10*time.Minute) is mounted globally at cmd/api/main.go:233 before route-level authMiddleware (cmd/api/main.go:240-241). 2) Redis key is formed solely from the header as "idempotency:" + key (internal/core/middleware/idempotency.go:63) without user/tenant, HTTP method, path, or request body digest scoping. 3) A victim sends a mutating request such as POST /account/login with Idempotency-Key: <key>, caching the TokenResponse (accessToken and refreshToken) in Redis for 10 minutes. 4) An unauthenticated attacker sends any mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to any path) with the same Idempotency-Key header; Idempotency replays the victim's cached headers and body and calls c.Abort() (lines 94-105) before AuthMiddleware or route handlers execute.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. Redis client is always initialized via redis.NewClient(cfg.Redis) at cmd/api/main.go:77. No upstream middleware scopes the key or authenticates prior to Idempotency.
findings.remediation: Scope the idempotency key by authenticated actor/tenant identity (when present, or require authentication on idempotent endpoints), HTTP method, normalized route path, and SHA-256 digest of the request body; reject key reuse with mismatched method/path/body (422/409); exclude authentication endpoints (/account/login, /account/refresh, /account/reset-password) or responses containing Set-Cookie/credentials; and mount Idempotency after AuthMiddleware for authenticated routes.

findings.title: Unrecovered Nil-Pointer Panic in Async Audit Logger When PostgreSQL Is Unavailable at Startup
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-476 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: 1) cmd/api/main.go:84-91 intentionally proceeds when database.Connect fails, leaving db == nil, and passes nil to audit.NewService(db, ...) at cmd/api/main.go:200. 2) An unauthenticated attacker sends POST /account/login. 3) account.Handler.Login calls h.repo.FindByEmail, which returns a nil-DB error (internal/modules/account/repository.go:63-65), causing Login to enter the failure branch and invoke h.audit.LogAsync(...) (internal/modules/account/handler.go:177-189). 4) The background worker goroutine in audit.NewService (internal/core/audit/service.go:47-54) runs outside middleware.Recovery and calls s.db.WithContext(ctx) at service.go:142, triggering an unrecovered nil-pointer panic that crashes the entire API process.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. middleware.Recovery (cmd/api/main.go:218) only protects the HTTP handler goroutine, not the background worker goroutine spawned in audit.NewService.
findings.remediation: Fail fast at startup in production when PostgreSQL is required, or guard s.db == nil in audit.service.Log (internal/core/audit/service.go:142) and add panic recovery inside the background audit worker goroutine (lines 47-54).

findings.title: Unconfigured Gin Trusted Proxies and Unvalidated ExtractClientIP Allow Rate-Limit/Budget Bypass and Audit Log Dropping
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-290 / CWE-348 / OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
findings.exploit_path: 1) cmd/api/main.go:212 initializes gin.New() without calling router.SetTrustedProxies(...), so Gin v1.10.0 trusts X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP from any client (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0). 2) Unauthenticated callers rotate spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers to bypass IP-based RateLimitWithLimiter (cmd/api/main.go:227-232, internal/core/ratelimit/limiter.go:170-175) and unauthenticated GraphQL BudgetTracker limits (internal/core/graphql/handler.go:447). 3) Additionally, AuditContext (cmd/api/main.go:216) uses ExtractClientIP (internal/core/middleware/audit.go:30-49), which accepts arbitrary unparsed strings from X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP; sending >45 chars causes INSERT into audit_logs.ip_address VARCHAR(45) (migrations/000005_create_audit_logs_table.up.sql:8) to fail, and audit/service.go:51 discards the error.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed for live rate limiting, GraphQL budget tracking, and audit log IP spoofing/drop. (GeoIPFilter in internal/core/security/geoip.go:154-172 would also be affected if wired, though it is currently unused in cmd/api/main.go.)
findings.remediation: Explicitly configure router.SetTrustedProxies(cfg.HTTP.TrustedProxies) (defaulting to nil / disabled unless behind a known proxy CIDR); replace ExtractClientIP's raw header parsing with c.ClientIP() (and validate with net.ParseIP / truncate or reject invalid values before persistence).

findings.title: GraphQL Exponential Fragment DAG Traversal Causes Unauthenticated CPU DoS
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-400 / CWE-1333 / OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
findings.exploit_path: 1) POST /graphql is mounted without authentication at cmd/api/main.go:244. 2) gqlparser validator.Validate (internal/core/graphql/handler.go:237) rejects cyclic fragments but permits non-cyclic fragment DAGs with aliased or repeated fragment spreads (e.g., 25-30 fragments F1..F30 where Fi spreads Fi+1 twice via aliases). 3) DepthEngine.calculateSelectionSetDepth (internal/core/graphql/complexity.go:73-84) and ComplexityEngine.calculateSelectionSetComplexity (complexity.go:173-181) clear visited[s.Name] = false on return without memoization and never short-circuit when MaxDepth or MaxComplexity is exceeded or when ctx.Done() fires, causing O(2^N) recursive traversal and CPU exhaustion.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. Verified gqlparser v2.5.16 only blocks cycles in no_fragment_cycles.go and memoizes its own walk, whereas DepthEngine and ComplexityEngine re-traverse every DAG path before limits reject the query.
findings.remediation: Memoize per-fragment depth and complexity results (and/or reject duplicate fragment spreads or bound total AST node expansions with a hard counter + early return once MaxDepth/MaxComplexity is exceeded), and check ctx.Done() during traversal.

findings.title: Existing Access and Refresh JWTs Remain Valid After Password Change or Password Reset
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-613 / OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.exploit_path: 1) An attacker obtains a victim's refresh token (7-day default TTL in internal/config/config.go:56) or access token (15-min default TTL). 2) The victim changes their password via POST /account/change-password (internal/modules/account/handler.go:343-398) or resets it via POST /account/reset-password (handler.go:466-513). 3) Neither handler revokes existing tokens, nor does TokenManager (internal/core/auth/token.go:58-63) track per-user token revocation timestamps (password_changed_at / token_version). 4) The attacker continues calling POST /account/refresh (handler.go:257-285) to mint fresh access and refresh tokens indefinitely.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. Refresh only checks JTI revocation and user.Status != "active" (handler.go:264), so pre-reset tokens remain valid until natural 7-day expiry.
findings.remediation: Persist a password_changed_at timestamp or monotonic token_version per user (cached in Redis or checked in Refresh/AuthMiddleware), reject tokens whose iat precedes password_changed_at (or mismatched token_version), and revoke active sessions upon password change or reset.

findings.title: Client-Controlled X-API-Priority and X-Priority Headers Bypass Overload Shedding
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-290 / CWE-770 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: 1) middleware.InboundOverload(overloadMgr) is registered globally at cmd/api/main.go:226 before RateLimitWithLimiter and route-level AuthMiddleware. 2) ExtractPriority (internal/core/overload/manager.go:334-339) trusts raw X-API-Priority and X-Priority headers from any unauthenticated client before checking routePriorities. 3) Sending X-Priority: critical triggers PriorityCritical in TryAcquire (manager.go:203, 230-237), bypassing memory/GC pressure shedding and claiming the 125% emergency capacity reserve.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. No upstream middleware strips or overwrites X-API-Priority or X-Priority, and no route-level WithPriority middleware is wired in cmd/api/main.go.
findings.remediation: Remove client-supplied X-API-Priority / X-Priority header trust from ExtractPriority (or gate header overrides behind a trusted internal gateway/HMAC signature) so priority is determined strictly from server-side route registration or authenticated claims.

findings.title: Refresh Handler Ignores RevokeToken Errors Enabling Refresh Token Replay
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-613 / CWE-252 / OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.exploit_path: 1) In POST /account/refresh (internal/modules/account/handler.go:269-280), ValidateRefreshToken checks Redis EXISTS (token.go:252), then Postgres FindByID runs (handler.go:263), and finally line 277 executes _ = h.tokenManager.RevokeToken(...) while discarding the error. 2) If Redis write fails (e.g., transient disconnect, READONLY failover, OOM) or concurrent refresh requests race between EXISTS and SET, Refresh still returns 200 OK with a new token pair without revoking the old refresh token, permitting token replay.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed for ignored RevokeToken error and concurrent check-then-set window. (The sub-claim regarding empty claims.ID was mitigated for external attackers by RS256 signing and uuid.NewString() in GenerateTokenPair, though ValidateRefreshToken/Refresh should still fail closed if claims.ID is empty.)
findings.remediation: Check and fail closed on h.tokenManager.RevokeToken errors (matching internal/core/auth/service.go:97-99), require non-empty claims.ID in ValidateAccessToken/ValidateRefreshToken, and make refresh-token consumption atomic (e.g., Redis SET NX / Lua check-and-revoke).

findings.title: Password Reset TOCTOU Race Condition and Ignored Token Consumption Error
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-362 / CWE-640 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: 1) POST /account/reset-password calls h.repo.FindValidPasswordReset (internal/modules/account/handler.go:481), which performs a non-locking SELECT (internal/modules/account/repository.go:125-127). 2) handler.go:487 runs Argon2id hashing (tens to hundreds of ms), widening the race window before UpdatePassword (line 493) and _ = h.repo.MarkPasswordResetUsed (line 498), whose error is discarded. 3) Concurrent requests with the same valid reset token can both pass validation and both overwrite the user's password, or a MarkPasswordResetUsed DB failure leaves the token reusable for its 15-minute TTL.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. No DB transaction or atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL RETURNING guards the password reset flow.
findings.remediation: Wrap ResetPassword's DB update in a transaction that atomically claims the reset token first via UPDATE password_resets SET used_at = NOW() WHERE token_hash = ? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW(), check rows affected/errors before updating the user's password, and fail closed if marking used fails.

findings.title: ForgotPassword Dispatches Empty Email Body Without Token and SMTPMailer Ignores Context Deadlines
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-640 / CWE-400 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: 1) POST /account/forgot-password (internal/modules/account/handler.go:442-450) invokes _ = h.mailer.Send(...) passing only Data: map[string]any{"Token": rawToken} with empty BodyHTML, BodyText, and TemplateName, and ignores delivery errors. 2) SMTPMailer.Send (internal/core/email/smtp.go:56-62) ignores TemplateName and Data, sending an empty email body without the reset token, and ignores ctx completely while blocking on net/smtp.SendMail—bypassing RequestDeadline (30s) if the SMTP server hangs and creating an observable timing discrepancy between existing and non-existent accounts.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed for empty email body, ignored errors, and ignored ctx timeout. (The CRLF header-injection sub-claim in smtp.go:43-53 is disproved as currently exploitable because Subject is hardcoded in handler.go:445, From comes from env config, and net/smtp.SendMail validates To/From against CR/LF.)
findings.remediation: Render a password reset body/template in ForgotPassword (or SMTPMailer), dispatch email asynchronously via the outbox/background job worker so ForgotPassword timing and error handling remain constant-time, enforce ctx deadlines via net.Dialer.DialContext + smtp.NewClient, and sanitize CR/LF in all email headers in SMTPMailer as defense-in-depth.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GraphQL, Playground/GraphiQL, and Swagger Endpoints Exposed in Production Mode
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-306 / CWE-200 / OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
findings.exploit_path: 1) cmd/api/main.go:238 calls registerSwagger(router) (cmd/api/swagger.go:12-13) and cmd/api/main.go:244 calls gqlHandler.RegisterRoutes(router) (internal/core/graphql/handler.go:165-170) unconditionally regardless of cfg.App.Env and without authMiddleware. 2) Any unauthenticated client in production can access /swagger/doc.json, /swagger/index.html, /playground, /graphiql, and GET/POST /graphql.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. Default GraphQL resolvers currently return static mock data and __schema introspection has no registered resolver, limiting immediate PII exposure, but production API schema disclosure and unauthenticated GraphQL query execution (amplifying SEC-AUD-004) are directly exposed.
findings.remediation: Gate Swagger UI (/swagger/*any) and GraphQL Playground/GraphiQL (/playground, /graphiql) behind non-production environments (cfg.App.Env == "development" || cfg.App.Env == "staging") and/or admin authentication, and require authMiddleware on /graphql (or explicit public allowlisting per operation).

findings.title: Unauthenticated /health Discloses Raw Dependency Errors and Runtime Stats; OTel Defaults to Plaintext gRPC
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-209 / CWE-319 / OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
findings.exploit_path: 1) healthChecker.RegisterRoutes(router) (cmd/api/main.go:237) exposes GET /health publicly without authMiddleware; HandleHealth (internal/core/telemetry/health.go:204, 209, 231, 252, 267-292, 307) returns raw driver/connection error strings from Postgres/Redis/Mongo and Go runtime memory/goroutine telemetry to unauthenticated callers. 2) InitTracer (internal/core/telemetry/otel.go:60-62) appends otlptracegrpc.WithInsecure() whenever OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is given as host:port without https://, transmitting trace spans in cleartext.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed on both wired paths (cmd/api/main.go:66, 237).
findings.remediation: Return only sanitized UP/DOWN status on unauthenticated /health (or move detailed dependency errors and SystemStats behind authenticated/internal admin health routes), leaving /health/live and /health/ready minimal for ALB probes; require TLS by default in InitTracer unless an explicit insecure opt-in env flag is set.

findings.title: Missing Global HTTP Body Size Limit, Unbounded Login Password, and Plaintext DB/Redis Transport Defaults
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-770 / CWE-319 / OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
findings.exploit_path: 1) Neither server.New (internal/core/server/server.go:73-80) nor the Gin middleware stack (cmd/api/main.go:214-234) enforces http.MaxBytesReader on REST endpoints (unlike GraphQL's 2MB cap at graphql/handler.go:193). 2) Unauthenticated clients can POST multi-megabyte JSON payloads to /account/* routes, and LoginRequest.Password (internal/modules/account/model.go:110) has no max length tag before entering Argon2id VerifyPasswordContext. 3) Additionally, DatabaseConfig.SSLMode defaults to "disable" (internal/config/config.go:74, internal/platform/database/postgres.go:29) and RedisConfig/NewClient (internal/platform/redis/redis.go:51-65) provides no TLSConfig option.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. RegisterRequest/ChangePasswordRequest/ResetPasswordRequest validate max=128 only after ShouldBindJSON has buffered the full body, and LoginRequest has no max bound at all.
findings.remediation: Add a global HTTP request body size limit middleware using http.MaxBytesReader (e.g., 1MB default for JSON APIs) and add max=128 validation on LoginRequest.Password and ChangePasswordRequest.OldPassword; default POSTGRES_SSLMODE to require in non-development environments and add TLSConfig support to RedisConfig/redis.NewClient.

findings.title: Silent Audit Log Drops on Oversized TargetID/IPAddress or Full Queue and Logger PII Masking Gaps
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-778 / CWE-532 / OWASP A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.exploit_path: 1) account.Handler.Login passes req.Email (up to 254+ chars under binding:"required,email") into audit.Entry.TargetID (internal/modules/account/handler.go:183), and AuditContext passes unvalidated X-Forwarded-For into IPAddress (handler.go:184, 207, 391, 506). 2) migrations/000005_create_audit_logs_table.up.sql:7-8 restricts target_id to VARCHAR(64) and ip_address to VARCHAR(45); oversized inputs cause Postgres SQLSTATE 22001 errors that audit/service.go:51 silently discards (_ = s.Log(ctx, entry)). 3) LogAsync (service.go:146-152) silently drops entries when the 1000-item buffer fills. 4) logger.MaskPII (internal/platform/logger/logger.go:14-19) does not redact password_hash, Authorization: Basic, or single-label host DSNs (e.g., postgres://user:pass@postgres:5432/db).
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed for audit log drops and MaskPII regex gaps. (audit.ScrubMap at service.go:60-108 only handles map[string]any/[]any, though no current handler passes Entry.Changes.)
findings.remediation: Validate/truncate IPAddress and use user/hashed TargetID (not raw email) or widen columns; log/metricize audit persistence errors and queue drops instead of silently discarding them; expand logger.MaskPII patterns for password_hash, Basic auth, and URI credentials (scheme://user:pass@host); and recursively scrub arbitrary maps/structs in ScrubMap.

findings.title: Failing CI Security/Verify Stubs, Unpinned Container Base Images, and Unauthenticated Compose Datastores
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-1188 / CWE-1395 / OWASP A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components
findings.exploit_path: 1) .github/workflows/ci.yml:36-50 defines static-analysis and dependency-audit as unconfigured TODO stubs that exit 1, and scripts/verify-full.sh:7-8 exits 1 before ratchet.sh, leaving SAST and govulncheck/SCA disabled in CI. 2) Dockerfile:9, 51 references mutable tags (golang:1.23.3-alpine, alpine:3.20) without SHA-256 digests. 3) compose.yaml:61 mounts ./migrations (containing *.down.sql DROP TABLE scripts) directly into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d, and compose.yaml:68-85 binds unauthenticated Redis (6379) and MongoDB (27017) on 0.0.0.0.
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed by direct inspection of .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/verify-full.sh, Dockerfile, and compose.yaml.
findings.remediation: Implement govulncheck and golangci-lint/gosec in ci.yml and integrate/replace TODOs in verify-full.sh; pin Dockerfile base images by @sha256 digest; bind compose.yaml ports to 127.0.0.1 with authentication enabled and run migrations via cmd/migrate instead of mounting raw up/down SQL files into docker-entrypoint-initdb.d.

findings.title: Wildcard Default HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Permits Arbitrary Cross-Origin WebSockets and CORS Reads
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-942 / CWE-346 / OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
findings.exploit_path: 1) internal/config/config.go:47 defaults HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to "*". 2) cmd/api/main.go:174 passes cfg.HTTP.AllowedOrigins to websocket.NewHandler, overriding checkOrigin's safe same-origin fallback (internal/core/websocket/handler.go:143-155) and permitting any malicious origin to open WebSocket connections. 3) middleware.CORS (internal/core/middleware/cors.go:28-35) emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (without Allow-Credentials, limiting impact to unauthenticated endpoints such as /graphql and /swagger/doc.json).
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed as Low severity in the current Bearer-only architecture because CORS omits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials for * and WebSockets do not authenticate via cookies.
findings.remediation: Default HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to empty (fail-closed / same-origin only) in production and reject wildcard "*" when credentials or sensitive WebSocket origins are configured.

findings.title: WebSocket Auth Accepts JWTs via ?token= Query Parameter and NewHandler Fails Open When tokenManager Is Nil
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-598 / CWE-287 / OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.exploit_path: 1) internal/core/websocket/handler.go:117-120 prioritizes c.Query("token") for WebSocket handshake authentication on /realtime (cmd/api/main.go:243). Although StructuredLogger masks token= in app stdout logs (internal/platform/logger/logger.go:18), external ALB/reverse-proxy access logs, browser history, and Referer headers capture full query strings containing 15-minute access JWTs. 2) Additionally, HandleWebSocket (handler.go:86-89) falls back to ?user_id= if tokenManager == nil (mitigated in cmd/api/main.go:118-127, where tokenManager is non-nil).
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed ?token= query-string exposure in upstream proxies/ALB; disproved ?user_id= reachability in cmd/api/main.go because JWT keys are required and log.Fatal aborts startup if tokenManager fails.
findings.remediation: Replace ?token= query-string JWTs with short-lived, single-use opaque WebSocket handshake tickets (stored in Redis) or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol auth, and fail closed (500/401) in HandleWebSocket if tokenManager is nil.

findings.title: Production Binary Imports testing Package and Dead COOKIE_SECRET / Session-Unbound CSRFMiddleware
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-489 / CWE-352 / OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
findings.exploit_path: 1) internal/core/jobs/ledger.go:10 imports "testing" for NewTestLedger (line 353), which is compiled into cmd/worker (cmd/worker/main.go:13), registering Go test flags (-test.*) in the production worker CLI. 2) internal/config/config.go:54 marks COOKIE_SECRET required:"true" even though it is never read; meanwhile, internal/core/middleware/csrf.go:24-61 is unmounted in cmd/api/main.go and generates tokens without user/session binding (making them susceptible to cookie-tossing if ever mounted with cookie auth).
findings.disprover_notes: Confirmed. CSRFMiddleware weakness is dormant because auth uses Authorization: Bearer headers rather than cookies, while the testing package import is active in cmd/worker.
findings.remediation: Move NewTestLedger to a _test.go file (e.g., ledger_test.go or internal/testutil); bind CSRF tokens to an authenticated session/user identifier if cookie auth is introduced; and remove unused COOKIE_SECRET requirement until cookie sessions exist.

findings.title: Unwired FeatureFlag Empty-Rule Fail-Open and Cache Nil-Interface Panic (Latent Library Defects)
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-636 / CWE-476 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: Neither featureflag.Engine.IsEnabled nor cache.GetOrSet has any production caller in cmd/ or internal/ (cmd/api/main.go:152 discards cache.NewFromAppConfig and lines 155-158 only call featureEngine.Close()). If wired later, a flag with Enabled=true and an allow_users/allow_roles rule having an empty Values slice evaluates hasTargeting=false at engine.go:467-478 and fails open (returns true); cache.GetOrSet (cache.go:414) would panic on res.(T) only when T is a non-empty interface type and loader returns (nil, nil).
findings.disprover_notes: Rejected as an active vulnerability because both primitives are unreachable/unwired in cmd/api/main.go and cmd/worker/main.go, and cache.GetOrSet does not panic for concrete or pointer types.
findings.remediation: Treat len(flag.Rules) > 0 as hasTargeting=true in featureflag.Engine.evaluate so empty allowlists fail closed; guard res == nil in cache.GetOrSet before asserting res.(T).

findings.title: Unwired Security Primitives: GeoIP Fail-Open, UploadService Empty Allowlist, and Captcha Hostname Check
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-636 / CWE-434 / OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design
findings.exploit_path: GeoIPService/GeoIPFilter, UploadService, and CaptchaVerifier have zero callers outside internal/core/security/ and security_test.go. If wired later without safeguards: missing/empty/corrupt MMDB causes GeoIPService to fail open (geoip.go:40-59, 111-114); UploadService skips MIME checking when AllowedMIMEs is empty (upload.go:160-172); and CaptchaVerifier ignores HCaptchaResponse.Hostname (captcha.go:109-114).
findings.disprover_notes: Rejected as a live vulnerability because all three components are unwired boilerplate library primitives unreachable from cmd/api or cmd/worker.
findings.remediation: Fail closed in GeoIPService when AllowedCountries is non-empty and the MMDB cannot be loaded; require non-empty AllowedMIMEs in NewUploadService (or deny active content like text/html); and support expected hostname verification in CaptchaVerifier.

findings.title: Unwired httpclient Singleflight Header-Unscoped Keying and SlackService Raw Client
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-639 / CWE-918 / OWASP A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.exploit_path: cmd/api/main.go:153 discards httpclient.New(), and singleflightEnabled defaults to false (client.go:66-74). SlackService uses raw http.Client (internal/core/notification/slack.go:131-135), but WebhookURL comes exclusively from SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL env config (internal/config/config.go:166) with no attacker control.
findings.disprover_notes: Rejected because httpclient.Client has zero production callers and SlackService destination URL is not attacker-controlled.
findings.remediation: Include Authorization/Cookie/tenant headers (or disable singleflight for authenticated requests) in httpclient singleflight keying, cap buffered response size in executeWithRetryBuffered, and pass the SSRF-protected httpclient.New() into SlackService in cmd/api/main.go.

findings.title: Unwired Spoofable Rate-Limit Identifier Modes (Device Fingerprint and Guest Session)
findings.cwe_owasp: CWE-290 / OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.exploit_path: IdentifierDeviceFingerprint trusts raw X-Device-Fingerprint headers and IdentifierGuestSession trusts unsigned guest_session cookies (internal/core/ratelimit/limiter.go:198-216), which would allow trivial rate-limit bypass if wired. However, cmd/api/main.go:227-232 only wires ratelimit.IdentifierIP.
findings.disprover_notes: Rejected as a live vulnerability because neither identifier mode is wired anywhere outside unit tests (internal/core/ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go).
findings.remediation: Combine device fingerprint / guest session rate limits with IP limits or require HMAC-signed server-issued guest session cookies before wiring those identifier modes.
